title: Redesign keyboard and contrast scenarios for dense grids, legends, and compact controls
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
The current component library exhibits multiple accessibility gaps when used in dense layouts (compact tables, chart legends with filter pills, and multi-action rows). Issues observed during recent customer audits and QA: unpredictable focus order after virtualization, legend filter pills that lack clear focus states and aria-pressed semantics, contrast failures in high-contrast/dark-mode combinations, and no automated regression metrics for token changes.

Scope:
- Audit and remediate keyboard navigation and focus restoration for virtualized tables and dense list widgets.
- Provide semantic roles and aria- states for legend filter pills and grouped controls.
- Define and apply contrast delta thresholds for token changes; add color-blind-safe fallbacks and explicit contrast tokens for dark/high-contrast modes.
- Produce VPAT-ready evidence artifacts for the affected components and the patterns (snippet-level examples + testing matrix).
- Add unit and visual regression checks (axe core baseline + contrast delta reporting + Percy snapshots) to prevent future regressions.

Approach / Deliverables:
1) Design spec: keyboard flow diagrams, focus traps vs. wrapping behavior for dense tables, and exemplar markup for aria-describedby/aria-owns patterns.
2) Token proposal: two new contrast tokens (control-contrast-strong, control-contrast-weak) with mapped values for light/dark/high-contrast palettes. Include a mapping table showing delta vs. current tokens.
3) Component updates: table row focus zone, legend filter pills (button role with aria-pressed), chart tooltip focus management, compact dropdown keyboard affordances.
4) Tests & artifacts: automated contrast checks in CI, a small user-testing script for keyboard-only flows, and VPAT evidence package (snippets, test results, screenshots).

Acceptance criteria:
- Keyboard-only walkthroughs for the dense table and legend widget pass with no missed focus stops in 3 hand-tested scenarios (pagination, sorting, and virtual scroll).
- Legend filter pills expose role="button" (or toggle) with aria-pressed updated and visible focus ring complying with WCAG 2.1 AA contrast.
- Contrast regression tool reports delta < 0.03 for token changes, and all updated controls meet 4.5:1 for regular text and 3:1 for UI components where applicable.
- VPAT package uploaded to Confluence (link in comments) with annotated screenshots and test commands.
- Engineering PRs include unit tests for new tokens, and visual snapshots for light/dark/compact densities.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Slight visual density change when enforcing stronger focus rings in compact contexts; will require design sign-off.
- Adding extra tokens increases maintenance surface; mitigate by documenting usage patterns and adding automated token linting.

Notes:
- This ticket intentionally focuses on patterns that affect both small controls and dense data surfaces; it should not attempt to rework the entire design system accessibility foundation (that is tracked under DES-110420).
